data.title: FTC Sues to Block Proposed $3.5 Billion Covetrus-MWI Merger
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Covetrus has been sued by the Federal Trade Commission to block the company from acquiring rival MWI Veterinary Supply.

Covetrus, which provides supplies to veterinarians, agreed in February to acquire Cencora's MWI animal-health business in a deal worth $3.5 billion.

The FTC is alleging the transaction would merge two of the biggest suppliers in the vet-clinic distribution industry, potentially driving up costs and hurting competition.

Covetrus responded to the suit Friday saying the merger would improve the economics of veterinary practices. By combining, Covetrus and MWI would make it easier and more efficient for vets to access products, the company said.

In its suit, the FTC said the emergence of Vetcove, an online platform allowing vets to compare prices across distributors, has fueled more pricing competition among suppliers. The market concentration that would allegedly occur from a merger renders the deal unlawful under antitrust law, the FTC said.

The FTC vote to authorize staff to seek a permanent injunction to block the proposed deal was 2-0.

Covetrus said it was confident in the merits of the proposed deal and that it was prepared to defend them in court.

data.title: Stocks fall with tech, Nvidia concerns; US dollar climbs
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq leads Wall Street indexes lower
  • Oil prices on track for 2nd weekly fall
  • Dollar extends gains for 4th day

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Elizabeth Howcroft

Stock indexes were mostly lower on Friday as technology shares sold off amid fresh concerns about US chipmaker Nvidia , while the dollar climbed to a fresh 19-month high.

The Nasdaq fell more than 1%, leading declines on Wall Street, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index down 4% and shares of Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom sharply lower. Nvidia shares were down 3%.

Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday as Nvidia CEO could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI industry and supply chain given his push to preserve access to the Chinese market and close ties with US President Donald Trump.

The US Justice Department said it does not know whether the Chinese businesswoman at the center of the scandal was a spy.

Inflation worries remained in focus. Investors absorbed a report showing the US October Producer Price Index for final demand was slightly softer than expected, but still shot up 6.5% year over year. It followed a hotter-than-expected US consumer prices reading earlier this week.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 120.15 points, or 0.23%, to 52,176.94, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 63.99 points, or 0.84%, to 7,528.41 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 356.51 points, or 1.40%, to 25,009.58.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 7.66 points, or 0.69%, to 1,108.61. The pan-European STOXX 600 index ended up 0.02%, registering a gain for the week.

AI-related shares in China dropped after Huang's exit, but indexes in Taiwan, Japan and South Korea gained overnight as traders played down concerns about its impact on the AI boom.

A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was still affecting communications for businesses and governments globally on Friday, forcing some to revert to fax machines and halting at least one bond repurchase in Europe.

US 2-YEAR YIELDS HEAD FOR LARGEST WEEKLY RISE IN OVER TWO YEARS

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro,

rose 0.13% to 103.35, and hit its highest level since April 2025. It was also on track for a fourth straight day of gains.

The euro was down 0.17% at $1.1034. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.03% to 159.9.

Treasury yields briefly dipped after the PPI data, but interest-rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields were on track for the largest weekly increase in over two years.

Traders this week have been ramping up bets on faster interest rate increases following the consumer price data and hawkish Federal Reserve official commentary.

"Inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed's going to need to act a little bit quicker and a little bit more aggressively," said Molly Brooks, US rates strategist at TD Securities.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in an 11% chance of a 50-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting, which was seen as having zero probability a week ago, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch Tool.

The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield was last down 0.94 basis point at 4.855%. It earlier reached 4.892%, the highest since October 14, and is headed for the biggest weekly increase since the first week of October 2024.

Oil prices edged lower and were set for a second straight weekly decline as Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict. US crude fell 0.34% to $88.44 a barrel and Brent fell to $95.70 per barrel, down 0.14% on the day.

data.title: Soybean futures set two-week high, wheat rises from June low
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures set a two-week high on Friday and corn futures also advanced as traders refocused on tightened US supply forecasts.

The US Department of Agriculture lowered its projection for 2026-27 soybean ending stocks in a monthly report on Tuesday, when analysts were expecting an increase. It also pegged US corn stocks below analysts' expectations.

"We're still digesting the report from earlier in the week," said Matt Wiegand, commodity broker for FuturesOne. "We got friendlier carryout numbers on corn and beans."

Most-active CBOT soybeans were up 13-1/2 cents at $12.32-1/2 a bushel and reached their highest level since October 30 at $12.40-3/4 in afternoon trading. Corn futures rose 3-1/2 cents to $4.46 a bushel, while wheat was up 9 cents at $5.93-1/4 a bushel after earlier falling to its lowest since June 30 at $5.82.

Technical buying helped to support the rebound in wheat, traders said.

This week, a surge in the dollar index to a 19-month high pressured US grains by making them look more expensive overseas. Some traders said losses on Thursday were overdone.

"Grains are bouncing strongly after yesterday's sharp selloff," said Andrey Sizov, head of consultancy Sovecon.

The USDA on Friday reported that exporters sold US soybeans to China, Vietnam and unknown destinations and US corn to Mexico.

Traders monitored continued disruptions to Black Sea grain exports, despite diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine.

With no sign of progress in Russia-Ukraine talks toward a ceasefire in the Black Sea, limited shipments should support wheat prices, Sizov said. He added that competitively priced new-crop Argentine wheat could remain a cap on prices.

"If wheat starts flowing through the Black Sea, there's likely more downside for prices," said Rod Baker, an analyst at Bendigo Bank. "If it doesn't, we're getting close to a price floor now."

data.title: Palo Alto Stock Upgraded to Buy After 20% Dip — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Investors can look past this week's chaos in the artificial-intelligence sector and find a steadier bet: cybersecurity. A Wall Street firm sees a prime buying opportunity in Palo Alto Networks ahead of the company's earnings report next week.

Shares of the cybersecurity giant have dropped roughly 20% over the past month. KeyBanc analyst Eric Heath says that pullback provides an ideal entry point ahead of an expected surge in corporate cybersecurity spending. The firm on Friday upgraded Palo Alto's shares to Overweight from Sector Weight with a $380 price target.

Investors appeared to shrug off the upgrade as cybersecurity stocks got caught up in a broader tech selloff Friday. Palo Alto Networks stock fell 0.7% to $320.45 Friday. Rivals CrowdStrike and Zscaler declined 2.1% and 0.6%, respectively.

Escalating AI-driven cyber threats have forced corporate security executives to open up their checkbooks. Cybersecurity spending is expected to grow over 20% in 2027, up from a single-digit pace in early 2026, as companies shift money toward major tech upgrades and AI security and away from routine maintenance, according to Heath.

At the same time, businesses increasingly want an "all-in-one" security provider rather than juggling dozens of separate tools. Palo Alto Networks, along with CrowdStrike, stand to benefit most from that trend, Heath noted. Smart bolt-on acquisitions have also given Palo Alto top-tier products across AI security and network defense, while its massive vault of proprietary data helps defend it from AI labs pushing into cybersecurity, Heath noted.

Not to mention, Palo Alto Networks has also been outselling its rivals, the analyst noted. He cited an industry partner who said: "I am hearing from vendors saying 'we are getting our butts kicked by Palo Alto because they really know how to sell the platform, have tremendous sales rigor, and keep stealing our customers.'"

KeyBanc's upgrade came as investor concerns have mounted over slowing demand for traditional network firewalls — a major legacy business for Palo Alto — as hardware upgrade cycles cool off and businesses shift toward cloud-based security. These fears flared after rival Fortinet recently delivered underwhelming third-quarter earnings.

But KeyBanc still sees other risks, including direct competition from major AI labs building their own security tools and the possibility that corporate budgets grow more slowly than expected.

Morgan Stanley analyst Meta Marshall also remains bullish on Palo Alto Networks heading into its fiscal-first-quarter earnings, maintaining an Overweight rating and $410 price target on shares. She expects management to raise its fiscal 2027 forecast for its next-generation security (referring to modern AI and cloud subscriptions) annual recurring revenue, a subscription metric closely watched by Wall Street to see how fast Palo Alto's AI and cloud products have grown.

Analysts polled by FactSet expect Palo Alto Networks to post adjusted earnings of 97 cents a share on revenue of $3.3 billion for the fiscal first quarter ended Oct. 31.

data.title: Nvidia Is Lending This AI Start-Up $2 Billion. Now Jensen Huang Is Gone, and an IPO Looms. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

As neocloud Nscale inches closer to an initial public offering, its growing debt load and complicated relationship with Nvidia raise questions about its valuation and IPO timing. The firm's IPO was already being closely watched as a barometer of the market's appetite for ongoing spending on the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.

The London-based company, which builds data centers and counts Anthropic, Microsoft, and Nvidia as major partners, disclosed in an amended prospectus dated Nov. 12 that it has deeper ties with Nvidia than previously known. It now says the artificial intelligence chip behemoth provided $2 billion of the $3.36 billion convertible loan announced in September, up from the $1 billion previously disclosed. (The second $1 billion closes "on or around" Nov. 16.)

The disclosure is important in light of the recent shake-up at Nvidia, which has rattled investors over concerns that without Jensen Huang, the company may lose some of its pull.

"Nvidia's leadership transition may make support more selective," Bloomberg Intelligence's Vasu Kasibhotla wrote in a Friday note. In other words, a new Nvidia CEO might be less willing to invest in debt-laden start-ups like Nscale.

While Nscale has more than $105 billion in total contract value, or customer deals, it also has more debt than cash on hand. It estimated in the new filing that, as of Sept. 30, its cash and cash equivalents were $3.6 billion, with debt of $5.5 billion.

Building out new data centers is expensive, and its circular financing deals with Nvidia could become riskier given the uncertainty around how Nvidia will handle such partnerships going forward. Nscale buys Nvidia chips for its data centers while also borrowing from Nvidia to build them.

Combined with ongoing fears about excessive spending on data centers by hyperscalers like Microsoft, with which Nscale signed agreements worth up to $43.8 billion before a $3.22 billion agreement was terminated, the latest disclosure could put more downward pressure on Nscale's valuation. Bloomberg previously reported that investors were pushing back on a possible $30 billion valuation — weeks before the Nvidia shake-up.

Nscale, which is in a quiet period, didn't respond to Barron's request for comment. Its IPO is expected later this year or in early 2027.

data.title: US energy firms cut rigs for first time in six weeks, says Baker Hughes
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino and Anjana Anil

US energy firms this week cut the number of rigs operating for the first time in six weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, fell by three to 601 in the week to November 13, the lowest since October 2. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Despite this week's rig decline, Baker Hughes said the total count was still up 52 rigs, or 9.5% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose were unchanged at 463 this week, while gas rigs fell by four to 127, their lowest since August, and other miscellaneous rigs rose by one to 11.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But now with spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 113.0 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

data.title: Anthropic sued for trademark infringement over 'Mythos' model
data.description:
By Blake Brittain

A software company called Mythos sued Anthropic in Virginia federal court on Friday, alleging the AI company's use of "Mythos" violates its trademark rights.

  • Mythos, which operates a software platform for nonprofit organizations, told the court that Anthropic's Mythos AI model will create market confusion and cause it "great and irreparable injury"

  • Mythos asked the court for an unspecified amount of monetary damages and a court order blocking Anthropic from using the "Mythos" name

  • "We disagree with the allegations in the complaint and intend to defend ourselves vigorously," an Anthropic spokesperson said

  • Anthropic released its powerful Mythos model in June after addressing US government concerns about potential national security risks

  • Alexandria, Virginia-based Mythos said that it launched its platform in 2015

  • The US Patent and Trademark Office rejected Anthropic's bid to register federal "Claude Mythos" trademarks in October based on likely confusion with Mythos, though that decision is not final

The case is Global Printing Inc d/b/a Mythos v. Anthropic PBC, US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, No. 1:26-cv-03756

For Mythos: Adam Hess of Squire Patton Boggs (US)

For Anthropic: attorney information not yet available

data.title: Why Microsoft Outage Is the Worst Possible Timing for the Stock — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown and Kit Norton

Microsoft is having a rough few days, not quite Nvidia levels of bad but far from ideal.

A global outage hit the company's Outlook, Teams, and Copilot AI assistant, impacting users across more than 70 countries, according to outage tracker Downdetector. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 services, as well as governments and organizations around the world.

The timing of the outage is particularly inconvenient for Microsoft. Anthropic launched a new suite of office tools on Tuesday and the market saw it as a direct challenge to the tech giant.

Engineers have been working to fix the problem for more than 20 hours. At 11:40 a.m. Eastern time Friday, the company again apologized for the disruption and said it was seeing "broad recovery and stability" across its services.

"Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," Microsoft said.

The company's updates illustrate it was a slog of an effort to restore services. Microsoft said in a status update shortly after 10 p.m. Thursday, more than nine hours after first confirming it was investigating the issue, that changes "applied to improve serviceability" weren't "taking as expected."

Over the intervening hours, however, Microsoft reported improvements in service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.

The company has also said the outage was a technical issue and wasn't related to cybersecurity or artificial-intelligence agents. Microsoft will provide a full post-incident report once the company's review is complete.

The stock rose 0.1% to $523.70 on Friday, recovering from a drop of more than 2% in the premarket session.

It's been a tough week for the tech giant. Reports of OpenAI's latest figures suggested that it's some way behind Anthropic in the AI race.

That's bad news for Microsoft, which has a 24% stake in the OpenAI and a much smaller investment in Anthropic.

Investors, however, might be in for some good news next week when the tech company holds its "Ignite" conference. Microsoft is expected to focus on advancements around its cloud platform, Azure, and Copilot.

"We expect the event to reinforce confidence in Microsoft's AI growth narrative," Citi analyst Tyler Radke said in a research note.

data.title: IIOT-OXYS Restructures Preferred Stock Obligations and Extends $75,000 Note
data.description:
IIOT-OXYS completed two preferred stock exchanges on November 6, 2026, converting an $84,262.65 reimbursement obligation to Scott Cox and exchanging all outstanding Series C preferred shares and related rights, valued at $76,408, for Series E shares. The transactions generated no cash proceeds and eliminated the Series C shares and exchanged obligations. The company also extended the maturity of its $75,000 GHS convertible note to April 30, 2027, with GHS waiving certain prior defaults.

Agreement 1: IIOT-OXYS Converts $84,263 Reimbursement Debt Into Series E Preferred Stock

  • Agreement type: Debt acknowledgment and preferred stock exchange
  • Counterparty: Scott Cox
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 06 2026 / Nov 06 2026
  • Duration / Termination: At will
  • Reason: Extinguish an existing reimbursement obligation without cash payment

Agreement 2: IIOT-OXYS Exchanges $76,408 of Series C Preferred Rights for Series E Shares

  • Agreement type: Series C preferred stock exchange
  • Counterparty: Clifford L. Emmons, Vivek Dave and Giro Di Biase
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 06 2026 / Nov 06 2026
  • Duration / Termination: At will
  • Reason: Replace outstanding Series C shares and related payment rights with Series E shares

Agreement 3: IIOT-OXYS Extends $75,000 GHS Convertible Note to April 2027

  • Agreement type: Convertible promissory note maturity extension
  • Counterparty: GHS Investments
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 06 2026 / Oct 31 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Extended maturity to Apr 30 2027
  • Reason: Extend note maturity and waive prior events of default

Original SEC Filing: IIOT-OXYS, Inc. [ ITOX ] - 8-K - Nov. 13, 2026
